children: Apple’s
first foldable iPhone has the potential to transform an experimental smartphone category into the industry standard, according to Bloomberg News reporter Mark Gurman.
Gurman described the new iPhone Duo as one of Apple’s

most consequential products, putting it just below landmark devices such as the iMac, iPod, iPad and Apple Watch. While foldable phones have existed for years, he said Apple’s combination of software, materials and durability gives the Duo a stronger chance of winning mainstream acceptance.

The $1,999 device also represents an important opening act for new Apple Chief Executive John Ternus. Former CEO Tim Cook could have introduced the product before moving into the executive chairman role, Gurman argued, but instead allowed his successor to take center stage.
New direction for the iPhone
Rather than replacing the iPhone with augmented-reality glasses or an artificial intelligence wearable, Apple
has reimagined the phone itself.

Gurman argued that AI assistants may eventually handle messages, appointments, research, email and calls. However, consumers will still need a powerful device with a substantial screen for activities such as reading, gaming, photography and videoconferencing.
That makes the foldable phone a possible bridge between the smartphone and tablet. Its larger display could also allow it to replace a laptop for some everyday tasks.
Apple
appears to have identified compelling reasons to buy the Duo from the outset, Gurman said. The company has emphasized video, gaming and photography while tailoring features to its folding design.

The second screen can serve as a camera viewfinder or FaceTime monitor. The phone also includes expanded widget capabilities and modes that take advantage of its ability to stand upright without a separate support.
That contrasts with the Vision Pro, an advanced but expensive headset whose limited consumer appeal made it a commercial disappointment. Apple
also initially struggled to define the Apple Watch before repositioning it around health and fitness.
Foldables could become the majority
Foldable devices currently represent about 2% of worldwide smartphone shipments, despite Samsung
introducing its Galaxy Fold seven years ago. Gurman predicts that foldables will account for most new phone sales within a decade.

He expects the iPhone Duo to become the leading foldable model by early next year, with demand producing severe shortages and sharply higher resale prices. Some buyers may also purchase the device in the United States for resale in countries where Apple
charges more.

The shift would probably happen more gradually than the original transition from conventional mobile phones to smartphones. The chief obstacle is price: The Duo starts at $1,999, more than the combined cost of two standard iPhones.
Gurman expects that barrier to diminish as component costs fall and Apple
expands its device-leasing program outside the United States. Monthly payments could eventually become a more important part of Apple’s marketing than the phone’s full retail price.
Foldable iPhone family may follow
Apple
is also unlikely to stop with one model. Gurman sees room for an entire family of foldable phones, potentially including a larger Duo Max and a less expensive Duo SE or Duo mini.
The Duo name gives Apple
greater flexibility to expand the lineup than a designation such as “iPhone Ultra,” which had been considered inside the company, according to Gurman.
Apple

may not control the foldable market indefinitely. Instead, Gurman expects the Duo to play a role similar to that of the original iPhone: establishing a product format that competitors adopt and improve.
For Apple

and its investors, the bigger opportunity is not merely selling a premium phone. If Gurman’s forecast proves accurate, the Duo could begin a lengthy replacement cycle, create a new high-priced iPhone tier and reinvigorate a global smartphone market that has struggled to generate genuinely new reasons for consumers to upgrade.

title: Apple’s foldable iPhone could make the format the new normal, Gurman says
